name: How the draft artifacts are authored (the product-truth agents)
summary: The agent pipeline behind define-a-feature's draft step: a classifier decides which artifacts a request needs, then only the required authoring agents run — a mock-data agent drafts or extends the one canonical dataset, a mockup agent draws the screens from that data, a flow agent assembles the journey wiring steps to screens and entities, and finally the business-analyst derives the acceptance criteria from the flow's steps. The handoff medium between agents is the artifact each produces plus the classifier's decision, so a single-screen tweak never spins up a whole journey and a backend job never drafts a screen. None of these agents exist yet — this flow is the spec for building them, so every step renders not-started.

steps.label: Classify what the request needs
steps.human: A classifier reads the plain-language request and decides which artifacts it needs — flow, mock data, mockups, or a subset — plus the target component and entities, so the pipeline only runs the agents that fit.

steps.label: Search the store (add vs create)
steps.human: Before drafting anything, the pipeline searches the product-truth index by component and entities to decide whether to extend an existing artifact or create a new one — there is one canonical dataset per entity per component.

steps.label: Mock-data agent drafts the data
steps.human: The mock-data agent drafts or extends the one canonical dataset for the classified entities — realistic records the mockups and flow are built on, never a duplicate dataset.

steps.label: Mockup agent draws the screens
steps.human: The mockup agent drafts each screen the request implies, populated from the drafted mock data, registering a screen id the flow's steps can resolve.

steps.label: Flow agent assembles the journey
steps.human: The flow agent assembles the draft flow, ordering the steps and wiring each to its screen and the entities it reads and writes, with an acceptance_scenario per step.

steps.label: Business-analyst derives the ACs
steps.human: Once the person approves the drafted flow, the business-analyst derives the L2/L3 acceptance criteria from the flow's steps and back-links each step via step.implements — the flow stays the reviewable source of truth.

branches.condition: classifier outcome = mockup+data (a single screen, not a journey)
branches.label: Skip the flow agent
branches.human: For a single-screen change the classifier returns mockup+data: the mock-data and mockup agents run, but the flow agent is skipped — there is no multi-step journey to assemble.

branches.label: Only the mock-data agent runs
branches.human: For backend logic, an API, or a batch job the classifier returns mock-data-only: just the mock-data agent runs so tests have realistic fixtures — no mockups, no flow.

branches.condition: classifier outcome = mockup-only (a static screen with no records)
branches.label: Only the mockup agent runs
branches.human: For a static screen with no business data (e.g. an About page) the classifier returns mockup-only: just the mockup agent runs — no dataset to draft, no journey.

branches.condition: classifier outcome = none (config / schema / docs, no product surface)
branches.label: Draft no artifacts
branches.human: For a config change, a schema/perf tweak, or documentation the classifier returns none: no product-truth artifacts are drafted and the request goes straight to normal AC authoring.

acceptance_scenarios.then: it returns which of flow / mock data / mockups the request needs, plus the component and entities

acceptance_scenarios.given: a classified request naming a component and entities
acceptance_scenarios.when: the pipeline searches the product-truth index
acceptance_scenarios.then: it decides to extend the existing canonical artifact or create a new one, never duplicating a dataset
the one canonical dataset for those entities is drafted or extended in place

acceptance_scenarios.given: drafted mock data and a request with screens
acceptance_scenarios.then: each screen is produced and populated from that mock data with a resolvable screen id
a draft flow is assembled with each step wired to its screen, its read/write entities, and an acceptance_scenario
acceptance criteria are derived from the flow's steps and each step is back-linked via step.implements
the mock-data and mockup agents run but the flow agent is skipped
no product-truth artifacts are drafted and the request goes straight to normal AC authoring

provenance.note: Real data-flow of the product-truth authoring agents (classify -> search -> mock data -> mockups -> flow -> derive ACs) with the agent + consumes/produces handoff contract and the classifier decision branches (mockup+data / mock-data-only / mockup-only / none). Specs the agents behind define-a-feature's draft step — none built yet, so all steps are not_started.
